info.title: API.SH: LeetCode
info.description: The LeetCode API from API.SH: public LeetCode data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
One LeetCode problem's metadata: number, title, link, difficulty, category, premium flag, likes and dislikes, accepted and total submissions, acceptance rate, topic tags, similar problems, number of hints, solution flags, languages offered, and the function name, parameter types and return type. The problem statement itself is not returned.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/leetcode-problem

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A LeetCode user's public profile: name, avatar, about, country, company, school, websites, skills, social links, ranking, reputation, post views, solutions, solved counts by difficulty (with the totals), streak and active days, badges, problems solved per language and per topic (advanced, intermediate, fundamental), and contest rating, attended contests, global ranking and top percentage. Also returns submission_calendar: submissions per day (date, submissions) for the last 12 months, or for one calendar year with year (which also scopes streak and active days); calendar_year echoes that year.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/leetcode-user

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: LeetCode username or leetcode.com/u/ profile link.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Calendar year for submission_calendar, streak and active days (a year listed in active_years). Default: the last 12 months.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
